current_disclosures.section: Products, Market, and Sales > Product Technologies
current_disclosures.summary: DRAM products are volatile, low-latency memory devices used in various markets including data centers, PCs, and automotive. In 2025, the company began shipping the industry's first 1γ production node incorporating EUV lithography for improved efficiency, while the majority of DRAM bit production remained on the 1ß node. This portfolio includes specialized types such as High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) for AI and high-performance computing, Double Data Rate (DDR) including DDR5, Low-Power DRAM (LPDDR) for mobile devices, and Graphics DRAM (GDDR) for graphics-intensive applications.

It also provides XR platform features (e.g., 6DoF tracking), automotive platform features (digital cockpit, ADAS), memory/controllers, fast charging, Smart Transmit technology, and power management systems.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and QCOM disclose the use of volatile memory technology within their respective semiconductor portfolios, though applied in different end-market contexts. MU explicitly defines its core DRAM products as volatile devices used in data centers and client PCs. QCOM describes its broader technology stack, which includes volatile LPDDR4 and LPDDR5 memory and controllers primarily utilized in mobile and automotive industries. While both address volatile memory, MU's focus is on the primary memory component for high-speed computing, whereas QCOM's mention is part of a broader connectivity and platform feature set including Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.

sentences.text: DRAM products lose content when power is turned off ("volatile") and are most commonly used in the data center, client PC, graphics, industrial, and automotive markets.
